title: Micro-commitment Slots & Backpressure Hedge — PRD (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a lightweight, operationally-friendly model for allocating tiny, timeboxed "micro-commitment" slots to tenants of Dedicated pools to provide deterministic burst capacity without long-lived reservations. The mechanism is intended to reduce failed requests during sudden demand spikes, limit noisy-neighbor impact, and provide predictable fallbacks to hosted or lower-fidelity model variants when needed.

Problem statement (concise):
- Dedicated customers want burst headroom for sporadic, latency-sensitive peaks but don’t want to pay for larger reserved capacity.
- Current burst systems either: (a) hand out transient capacity unpredictably, or (b) require large-scale warm pools with heavy cost.
- Noisy tenants can cause tail-latency cascades; hard isolation is expensive. We need a middle path: cheap, predictable, and auditable micro-reservations that integrate with autoscaling/backpressure.

Goals:
- Provide sub-minute micro-commitments that hold a small amount of compute (eg. 0.5–5% of a slot) for a short duration (15–120s).
- Integrate with autoscaler signals so micro-commitments are granted proactively when telemetry predicts a spike.
- Implement soft isolation semantics: capacity guaranteed for slot duration, with defined degradation policies (queue / fallback) when commitments are exhausted.
- Keep accounting simple for billing/credits and provide clear telemetry for customers and SRE.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-term reserved capacity commitments or larger dedicated pool purchases.
- Not intended to provide unlimited burst capacity — we intentionally cap aggregate micro-commitment availability per pool.

User stories:
- As a product engineer at Acme, I want a 30s micro-slot so scheduled jobs can tolerate sudden traffic bursts without failing 95th pct requests.
- As an SRE, I want visibility into micro-commit allocation/eviction and a simple knob to disable micro-commitments during incidents.
- As a billing manager, I want to see clear micro-commit consumption and the option to purchase higher micro-commit budgets.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Micro-commitment (micro-slot): a time-limited guarantee that a tenant can use a small fraction of pool capacity for burst traffic.
- Burst-hedge pool: a logical cap that defines how much micro-capacity the entire Dedicated pool will expose.
- Hedging credit: internal accounting token used to bill/track micro-commit usage.
- Soft-eviction: gracefully degrade to queued requests, hosted fallback, or lower-fidelity model when micro-slots exhausted.

Design overview:
1) Admission: Tenants request micro-slots via API/SDK or automatically via router policy when a request would breach latency SLO. The request includes desired duration and compute weight.
2) Granting: A micro-commit broker consults recent telemetry (RPS delta, queue growth, tail latency) + pool budget and either grants, delays, or denies the micro-slot.
3) Enforcement: Granted micro-slots tag incoming requests for priority scheduling and KV cache affinity for the slot duration.
4) Charge & settle: Assign hedging credits at grant time (small upfront token). Final charge reconciles on actual consumption (per-token or per-second usage).
5) Eviction & fallback: If pool reclaim needed, soft-evict micro-slots in least-recently-granted order with clear inkling to customer (webhook/metric).

Autoscaling interactions:
- Predictive grants: Autoscaler exposes a short-horizon spike probability (0–100%). We translate probability bands to conservative micro-commit budgets (eg. 30% chance => allocate up to 1% pool as micro-slots).
- Scale-up suppression: When many micro-slots are active, autoscaler is nudged to scale faster (prefer warm nodes over denying customers).
- Scale-down safety: Micro-commit usage counts against cool-down windows to avoid oscillation.

Burst credit economics:
- Hedging credits come in two forms: free baseline (included in subscription) + paid top-up. Baseline is deliberately small to encourage measured use.
- Pricing model options to consider: per-minute micro-slot, per-second compute-weight, or a hybrid with discount tiers for enterprise contracts.
- Billing events: grant, peak-consume, revoke. Provide breakdown in console and per-request labels for customer chargeback.

Isolation controls & fairness:
- Per-tenant soft-cap: individual tenant cannot hold > X micro-slots concurrently (configurable).
- Pool-level cap: prevent micro-commitments from exceeding Y% of total pool capacity.
- Noisy neighbor mitigation: if a tenant exceeds thresholds (error rate, tail latency), auto-throttle micro-slot grants and mark tenant for probation.
- Emergency shutter: SRE can disable micro-commit granting globally/for a pool/for a tenant via Console and API.

Observability & APIs:
- Metrics to emit: micro_slots_granted_total, active_micro_slots, micro_slot_evictions, micro_slot_latency_p90/95/99, micro_slot_cost_estimate.
- Tracing: propagate micro-slot id in trace spans for end-to-end correlation.
- Console: timeline view of micro-slot grants per-tenant, alerting on anomalous grant rates.

Rollout plan (phased):
0) Lab POC: small testbed cluster with simulated tenants and gap testing. (Q1)
1) Beta: opt-in for selected customers with clear console toggles + SLAs N/A. (Q2)
2) Configurable tiers: baseline/free micro-credits + paid top-ups in Console. (Q3)
3) GA: full telemetry, billing integration, and autoscaler coupling. (Q4)

Operational runbook (high level):
- Incident: if pool-level active_micro_slots > threshold AND tail latency spikes -> set pool micro_commit_shutter = true, notify customers, scale-up immediate.
- Degraded grants: if broker is overloaded, degrade to host fallback policy (route to hosted variants or enqueue).
- Audit: daily job verifies micro-slot ledger reconciliation vs. metrics and flags anomalies.

Open questions & tradeoffs:
- Duration granularity: discrete buckets (15s/30s/60s/120s) vs arbitrary seconds. Simpler buckets reduce state/complexity.
- Billing friction: bill at grant vs bill at consumption. Upfront billing simplifies bookkeeping but is less fair.
- Warm cache benefits: should micro-slots pin KV cache entries? Advantageous for latency but increases state complexity.
- Contention model: should micro-slots preempt lower-priority queued requests? Implementation complexity vs customer expectations.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: micro-slots mask real capacity needs and delay purchases of necessary Reserved capacity.
  Mitigation: cap micro-slot utility and add usage alerts that recommend reserve purchases.
- Risk: greedy tenants exhaust pool hedge and cause outages.
  Mitigation: pool caps + emergency shutter + per-tenant probation model.
- Risk: complex billing disputes.
  Mitigation: full transparent ledger + trial period + granular per-request labels for customers.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Align with billing & legal on hedging credit model (owner: Ravi).
- Prototype broker flow and publish linear ticket for telemetry hooks (owner: Evelyn).
- Run tabletop incident simulations with SRE to validate emergency shutter semantics (owner: Diego).
- Design Console tiles and audit views (owner: Product-UX).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the initial feature small: discrete durations and low % pool cap. Avoid over-indexing on complex pricing early.
- Tie evictions to transparent webhook so customers can automate fallback.
- Link to RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/89 (early design notes)

Signed-off-by: Maya Thompson (product-dedicated)
